findings.text: validate_landing_patch keys the open-section guard on the requested status rather than on the transition, so a plan already at shipped or done that holds an open section is re-judged on the PATCH path (reckon/serve.py:3577) while the other two sites grandfather it — the brief and the evidence fragment both state an already-terminal plan is not re-judged. Reproduced against the reviewed head: validate_landing_patch on an already-done state whose s2 is implementable raises 'terminal status refused: 1 section(s) still open (s2)', where apply_ops on the same state returns without raising.

justifications.evidence: the manifest's tests line and base_arm.log record the census count (17 of 213 in the evidence fragment), the 5-passed head arm EXIT=0 and the 3-failed base arm EXIT=1, so the done_when's measure is recorded rather than claimed.
justifications.fit: reckon/_store.py:3251 adds _require_every_section_ticked in the existing _require_* terminal-guard idiom and reuses the pre-existing _LANDED_STATUSES constant (:3130) rather than a new status set.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/_store.py:3285 (validate_landing_patch), :1344 (_write_state_locked) and :3403 (apply_ops) call _require_every_section_ticked on a write moving a plan into shipped or done, and :3261 reads _plan_html.open_sections, so the landed change refuses the landing and names the open ids exactly as the goal states.
